The code is set up so clicking a marker opens the dialog. The `onClick` handler on the Marker component (lines 59-61) calls `onPlaceSelect`, which sets the selected place ID and opens the dialog.

The implementation should work. The `@vis.gl/react-google-maps` Marker component supports the `onClick` prop. When you click a marker on the map, it should:

1. Call `onPlaceSelect(place.googlePlaceId)`
2. Set the `selectedPlaceId` state
3. Open the `PlaceDetailsDialog` with the place details

If it still doesn't work, the Marker component might need a different event handler. Test it and let me know if you need a ref-based approach to attach the click listener directly to the underlying Google Maps marker instance.

Adding a click handler to the Map component to detect clicks on Google Maps default markers and identify the clicked place:


---

<tool-use data-tool-type="write" data-tool-name="search_replace">

<details><summary>Tool use: **search_replace** • Edit file: /Users/joba/Projects/Private/hackathon/gmapsplus/src/components/Map.tsx</summary>

```diff
@@ -34,4 +34,43 @@
      }
    }, [map, userPlaces]);
+ 
+   // Handle clicks on default Google Maps markers
+   useEffect(() =&gt; {
+     if (!map) return;
+ 
+     const handleMapClick = (event: google.maps.MapMouseEvent) =&gt; {
+       if (!event.latLng) return;
+ 
+       // Use PlacesService to find nearby places at the clicked location
+       const placesService = new google.maps.places.PlacesService(map);
+       const request = {
+         location: event.latLng,
+         radius: 50, // Search within 50 meters
+         type: "establishment",
+       };
+ 
+       placesService.nearbySearch(request, (results, status) =&gt; {
+         if (
+           status === google.maps.places.PlacesServiceStatus.OK &amp;&amp;
+           results &amp;&amp;
+           results.length &gt; 0
+         ) {
+           // Get the closest place
+           const place = results[0];
+           if (place.place_id) {
+             onPlaceSelect(place.place_id);
+           }
+         }
+       });
+     };
+
```

Implementation complete. Clicking on the map (including default Google Maps markers) will:

1. Detect the click location
2. Use PlacesService to find nearby places within 50 meters
3. If a place is found, open the dialog with that place's details

The click handler is attached to the map instance and will work for clicks on default Google Maps markers. If you click near a marker, it finds the closest place and opens the dialog, same as when selecting from Autocomplete.

Note: This triggers on any map click, not just marker clicks. If you click empty space, it won't find a place and nothing happens. If you want it to only trigger when clicking directly on markers, we can refine it further.
